subject: Private hosting: integration runway & rapid feasibility checklist

Subject: Private hosting feasibility — high level asks (Everwell)

Hi Tessa / Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, Everwell wants a private deployment option (VPC + optional on-prem appliance) for our internal claims-processing models. High-level asks:

- Network isolation (no internet egress).
- Customer-managed KMS / HSM for model keys.
- Audit logs for 12 months with export to our SIEM.
- Ability to pin model versions and control rollouts.
- SLA for latency percentiles (p95 < 450ms) and predictable throughput during business hours.

I've attached our short questionnaire to surface obvious blockers and our procurement contact (procurement@everwell.com) will follow up with contract/PO questions.

Can your team do a rapid feasibility scan and a minimal piloting path? We're on a tight procurement cycle and would like a 2–3 week initial readout.

Thanks,
Alice Reed
Director, IT Operations | Everwell Health

Date: Mon, 03 Jul 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private hosting feasibility — architecture notes

Quick architecture note dump (high level):

- Network: Customer-only peering (VPC or direct connect). We can support no-internet-egress but need to confirm whether Everwell requires zero egress at the appliance level (air-gapped) or only VPC-level isolation. Air-gapped support introduces build/test windows and additional QA for updates.

- KMS/HSM: We support external KMS for model keys, but full HSM integration (BYOH) will add 4–6 weeks to pilot by our estimates — hardware procurement + validation. For the pilot, propose escrowed-key flow (customer controls keys in their KMS; we do not retain plaintext).

- KV cache & model state: If Everwell wants persistent KV cache across restarts for lower cold-start latency, that'll require a small state store (S3-compatible or NFS) inside their network. That is feasible but changes runbook and backup requirements.

- Telemetry/logging: We can push audit logs and metrics to customer's syslog/SIEM, but retention beyond 90 days will need storage sizing and export pipelines. 12 months retention (their ask) is feasible if they accept exported storage on their side.

- Updates/rollouts: Canary is doable, but auto-fallback across model variants requires our control-plane connectivity for health signals. If they want fully offline rollouts, we will need an installable control agent on their network (adds ops work).

Blockers: Full air-gap + HSM + 12-month on-prem log retention + offline rollouts = significant ops and timeline impact (likely > 3 months and add dedicated infra engineering and validation).

Proposed minimal pilot: VPC peering, customer KMS (no HSM), exported logs to SIEM (customer storage for >90d), pin model versions, canary with cloud-side health control. Rough dev effort: 2 engineers (infra + runtime) for 3–4 weeks + 1 SRE for pilot run.

I'll update the scan spreadsheet with these rows.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee | Staff Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 03 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private hosting feasibility — capacity & staffing

Heads-up on capacity/staffing:

- Compute: For the pilot (single region, modest throughput), plan for a 2-GPU (A10G-equivalent) capacity group and a standby 1‑GPU node for failover. If Everwell wants p95 < 450ms for multi-tenant bursts, we need more aggressive headroom — call it 3x expected baseline.

- Ops staffing: Pilot requires one infra engineer (0.5 FTE) and one runtime engineer (0.5 FTE) dedicated for 4 weeks, plus oncall rotation coverage during the pilot (shared across team). Production SLA would need 2‑3 full-time SREs for 24x5 coverage depending on scale.

- Backups/DR: If persistent KV is used, plan regular snapshots to customer-managed storage; adds ~0.5 FTE to runbook for first 3 months.

Risks: If customer insists on air-gap and on-prem appliance inventory, staffing and hardware provisioning lead time is the dominant delay.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Infrastructure Services

Thanks all for the fast turnaround. Alice — summarizing what we can commit to for a 2–3 week initial readout and a minimal pilot recommendation: 

Committed rapid readout (by Jul 14):
- Architecture gaps and clear "no-go" items (Soojin)
- Pilot compute and staffing estimate (Karthik & Marcus)
- Security evidence checklist and temporary mitigations (Kimberly)
- Consolidated Q&A response to your questionnaire (Tessa)

Minimal pilot proposal (scope for proposal to procurement):
- VPC peering (no internet egress) + customer-managed KMS (no HSM for pilot)
- Exported logs to Everwell SIEM with 90-day retention on our side; customer to accept exported storage for 12 months
- Canary rollout with cloud-side health signals (no fully offline rollouts in pilot)
- 2x GPU capacity group for baseline; standby node for failover

Estimated pilot resourcing: 2 engineers (infra + runtime) at 0.5–0.75 FTE each for 4 weeks + 0.5 FTE SRE for runbook and monitoring. High-level cost estimate to be included in the customer proposal.

Next steps:
1) I'll finish the consolidated scan and a one-page exec summary and share by EOD Thursday (Jul 5).
2) If Everwell is comfortable with the pilot constraints above, procurement can use the pilot scope + proposed SOW to start PO conversations.
3) If Everwell insists on HSM or air-gap for pilot, we will provide a separate timeline and resource estimate (longer lead).
